transcript.text: panasonic nn h98 not heating anymore, any fix?

The NN-H98 is an inverter microwave, so 'not heating' usually points to either a setting issue or a fault with the internal high-voltage circuitry (most commonly the inverter board or magnetron). First, please check these two things:
1. Was it set to 100% Power? If it was on Defrost or a low power level, it will not heat fully.
2. When you press Start, does the light come on and the turntable spin, but there is no heat? If it runs normally but doesn't heat, this suggests a hardware fault in the high-voltage system. Please do not open the casing; microwave capacitors can hold a lethal charge even when unplugged. If the settings are correct and it still doesn't heat, you will need to contact Panasonic support or a qualified appliance engineer for repair.
[Safety panel] Don't remove the microwave's casing or try to repair it inside. Parts inside a microwave can hold a dangerous electric charge even after it's unplugged — have it checked by a qualified engineer.
its not nn h98, h98 is what the screen says when it stops. model on the back is NN-CD87KSBPQ. turntable spins and fan runs but stops after a few seconds with no heat

Because this involves internal components that store lethal electrical charges even when unplugged, this is not a safe repair to attempt yourself. The fact that it runs for only a few seconds before stopping suggests the system has detected an electrical failure and shut down to protect itself. You will need to contact Panasonic support or a qualified appliance engineer to replace the faulty high-voltage component.
